CITY COUNCIL MEETING FOR MARCH 30, 2022 AT 8:30 A.M. WILL
  TAKE PLACE SOLELY BY VIDEOCONFERENCE/TELECONFERENCE.

  City Council Meeting Policy:
  www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-
  Meeting-Policy.pdf

In order to facilitate public participation at meetings held solely by electronic means, the
City will accept public comment in the following manner:

1. During the meeting, members of the public may provide live public comment by
  submitting a speaker card prior to the start of public comment on that item, at the
  following webpage:

  www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment

  If a public comment speaker wishes to speak on more than one agenda item,
  please indicate so on the online form (multiple item speakers will be handled
  according to the process posted on the agenda and as specified in the City Council
  meeting policy). Public comments are limited to 3 minutes each, and the Mayor
  and City Council may limit this time if reasonable under the circumstances.

2. Speaker Card Help Line: If a public comment speaker needs assistance in
  completing a speaker card, please call the City Clerk’s Office at: (626) 744-4124.
  Help line will open 30 minutes prior to the posted start time of the meeting.

  After submitting a public speaker card, join the virtual meeting after the published
  start time with a computer, other electronic device, or by telephone. The same
  name or telephone number on the Speaker Card should be used for the virtual
  meeting in order to locate and unmute the speaker. Your phone call to the City
  Council meeting will be recorded as part of the City Council meeting. By staying
  on the line and making public comment during the City Council meeting, you are
  agreeing to have your phone call recorded.

  Computer or electronic devices, join the meeting at:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446

  Telephone only dial-in: 1-669-900-6833, Meeting ID: 161 482 446

3. Members of the public may submit correspondence of any length prior to the start of
  the meeting, at the following email address:

  correspondence@cityofpasadena.net
  Correspondence will be forwarded to the City Council prior to the start of the
  meeting, posted online, and made part of the legislative record for the item.
 LIVESTREAM WITH CAPTIONING IS AVAILABLE AT WWW.PASADENAMEDIA.ORG,
  AND ALSO AT WWW.CITYOFPASADENA.NET/COMMISSIONS/AGENDAS,

  TO HEAR A LIVE SPANISH TRANSLATION OF THE MEETING (LISTEN ONLY),
  PLEASE DIAL-IN 10 MINUTES PRIOR TO THE MEETING (8:20 A.M.):
  TOLL-FREE DIAL-IN: (888) 585-9008
  PARTICIPANT PASSCODE: 739-142-091, THEN #

IF YOU NEED A REASONABLE MODIFICATION OR ACCOMMODATION PURSUANT
  TO THE AMERICANS WITH DISABILITIES ACT
BECAUSE YOU ARE UNABLE TO PARTICIPATE ELECTRONICALLY AS SET FORTH
  ABOVE, CONTACT THE CITY CLERK’S OFFICE
  AS SOON AS POSSIBLE AT (626) 744-4124 OR
  CITYCLERK@CITYOFPASADENA.NET.
 LA REUNIÓN ESPECIAL DEL CONSEJO MUNICIPAL DEL 30 DE MARZO DE 2022
  A LAS 8:30 A.M. TENDRÁ LUGAR ÚNICAMENTE POR
  VIDEOCONFERENCIA/TELECONFERENCIA.

  City Council Meeting Policy:
  www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/wp-content/uploads/sites/21/City-Council-
  Meeting-Policy.pdf

Para facilitar la participación del público en reuniones realizadas únicamente por
medios electrónicos, la Ciudad aceptará comentarios del público de la siguiente
manera:

1. Durante la reunión, los miembros del público pueden hacer comentarios públicos
  en vivo presentando una tarjeta de oratoria antes del inicio del comentario sobre el
  artículo que se está tratando en el siguiente sitio web:

  www.cityofpasadena.net/city-clerk/public-comment

  Si un orador de comentario público desea hablar sobre más de un artículo del
  orden del día, le solicitamos que lo indique en el formulario en línea (los oradores
  sobre artículos múltiples se manejarán según el proceso publicado en la agenda y
  lo especificado en la política sobre las reuniones el Consejo Municipal). Los
  comentarios públicos se limitan a 3 minutos cada uno y el Alcalde y el Consejo
  Municipal pueden limitar este tiempo si lo consideran razonable para las
  circunstancias.

2. Línea de ayuda de la tarjeta de oratoria pública: Si un orador de comentario
  público necesita asistencia para completar su tarjeta, puede llamar a la Oficina del
  Secretario de la Ciudad al (626) 744-4124. La línea de ayuda abrirá 30 minutos
  antes del inicio de la reunión.
  Después de presentar una tarjeta de oratoria pública, únase a la reunión virtual a la
  hora de inicio publicada con una computadora, otro dispositivo electrónico o por
  teléfono. Debe usar el mismo nombre o número de teléfono de la tarjeta de oratoria
  para la reunión virtual de modo que se pueda ubicar y habilitar el audio para el
  orador. Su llamada telefónica a la reunión del Concejo Municipal se grabará como
  parte de la reunión del Concejo Municipal. Al permanecer en la línea y hacer
  comentarios públicos durante la reunión del Concejo Municipal, está aceptando que
  se grabe su llamada telefónica.

  Computadoras y dispositivos electrónicos pueden sumarse a la reunión en:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/161482446

  Número para ingresar a la reunión por teléfono: 1-669-900-6833, ID de la
  reunión: 161 482 446
 3. Los miembros del público pueden enviar correspondencia de cualquier longitud
  antes del inicio de la reunión a la siguiente dirección de correo electrónico:

  correspondence@cityofpasadena.net

  La correspondencia se enviará al Consejo Municipal antes del inicio de la reunión,
  se publicará en línea, y se incorporará al registro legislativo sobre el artículo.

CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 30, 2022 - 8:30 A.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL JOINT MEETING WITH
  LOS ANGELES COUNTY SUPERVISOR KATHRYN BARGER

  The special meeting was convened and held virtually by videoconference/teleconference.

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called to order the special joint meeting with Los
  Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger at 8:38 a.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Los Angeles County Supervisor
  Katheryn Barger.

ROLL CALL:
 Councilmembers:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

Councilmember Kennedy  UPDATE ON FUTURE WORK PLANNED FOR THE
connected to the meeting at  COMPLETION OF THE DEVIL'S GATE RESERVOIR
8:38 a.m.  RESTORATION PROJECT -  PRESENTED BY LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS

  Supervisor Barger and Keith Lilley, County of Los Angeles Water
  Resources Manager, provided introductory comments, and
  Keith Hala, Los Angeles County Public Works Stormwater
  Engineer, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the Devil's
  Gate Reservoir Restoration project, including information on
  construction, habitat restoration efforts, remaining work at the
  Southeast entrance, and ongoing public outreach, with all
  responding to questions.

  Mayor Gordo and the City Council thanked Supervisor Barger
  and her staff in addressing Pasadena residents' concerns
  related to the restoration project. Mayor Gordo and
  Councilmember Hampton spoke on the need to upgrade or
  replace the maintenance sheds on site at the Devil's Gate
  Reservoir.

Council Minutes  1  03/30/2022
   Councilmember Kennedy asked the Los Angeles County staff to
  provide copies of any reports related to contaminants found in
  the sediment/soil removed as part of the project.

  Councilmember Williams requested that the Los Angeles County
  staff continue to provide clear information related to on-going
  maintenance at Devil's Gate Reservoir for the community and
  the City Council.

  Supervisor Barger responded that her staff will provide regular
  updates including future Devil's Gate Reservoir maintenance to
  the City Council and staff for public dissemination.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  INFORMATION ON PARTNERSHIPS FOR PROVIDING
  HOMELESS SERVICES - PRESENTED BY PASADENA
  DIRECTOR OF HOUSING, WILLIAM HUANG AND LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY

  William Huang, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the
  City's and Los Angeles County's collaborative efforts to combat
  homelessness and responded to questions. Cheri Todoroff,
  CEO of Los Angeles County's Homeless Initiative, spoke in
  support of continued collaborative efforts with the City, and
  supported increased flexibility related to utilizing Citizens For
  Citizens (CFC) funds towards Pasadena's housing needs, and
  responded to questions.

  Lt. Geoffrey Deedrick, Los Angeles County Sheriff's Homeless
  Outreach Stabilization Team (HOST) lead, and Kimberly
  Barnette with Los Angeles Continuum of Care, provided
  information on HOST's outreach, services and humanitarian
  efforts in the Pasadena area provided to individuals in homeless
  encampments; and responded to questions.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the issue of transients and homeless
  individuals that loiter at the Metro Rail stations in the City, and
  asked Supervisor Barger for assistance connecting with Metro
  representatives for additional resources to maintain and secure
  the train stations. He also asked the Supervisor to provide a
  letter of support related to Regional Housing Trust bill in order to
  maximize housing resources between the cities of Glendale,
  Burbank and Pasadena. Mayor Gordo expressed concerns with
  the City of Pasadena not receiving its fair share of resources

Council Minutes  2  03/30/2022
   related to Measure H funds, and spoke on the need to address
  governance and resource allocation to ensure that City's like
  Pasadena are receiving such funds to address homelessness in
  their Cities.

  Councilmember Madison advocated for resources to place
  severely mentally ill and substance abuse homeless individuals
  into treatment or protective custody.

  Supervisor Barger responded that Governor Gavin Newsom is
  taking up the issue and is currently considering a "care port" that
  will possibly include conservatorship, noting that L.A. County is
  currently building capacity to address homeless individuals that
  are severely mentally ill and in need of assistance under Welfare
Councilmember Williams was  and Institutions Code Section 5150 and working with state
excused and disconnected  legislatures to change laws to better serve those individuals.
from the meeting at 9:46 a.m.
  Vice Mayor Wilson advocated for additional robust tools and
  creative methods including tiny homes and allowing affordable
  housing on congregational land to help severely mentally ill and
  substance abuse homeless individuals in the City.

  Councilmember Kennedy asked Interim City Manager Kurtz to
  provide information on funding related to the New Pasadena
  Outreach Response Team (PORT) at the next City Council
  meeting.

  Mayor Gordo reported that he reached out to Jonathan E.
  Sherin, M.D., Director of Los Angeles County Department of
  Mental Health, and invited him to attend a City Council meeting
  to discuss mental health issues in the community.

  The following individuals provided comments on the item:

  Sonja Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Carl Selkin, representing Social Justice Committee,
  Pasadena, Jewish Temple and Center
  Alexander Boekelheide, representing Pasadena City
  College
  Pastor Kerwin Manning, Pasadena resident
  Areta Crowell, Pasadena resident
  Heavenly Hughes, representing My TRIBE Rise

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

Council Minutes  3  03/30/2022
   UPDATE ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY  MEASURE  J,  "ALTERNATIVE  TO
  INCARCERATION CHARTER AMENDMENT" - PRESENTED
  BY LOS ANGELES COUNTY

  Supervisor Barger summarized the provisions of Measure J
  approved by voters, and which dedicates funding to community
  programs for youth development, job training, small business
  development, supportive housing, services and alternatives to
  incarceration. She noted that Measure J is now called Care First
  Community Investment; provided information on how the City
  can apply for such funds; and responded to questions.

  The following individuals provided comments on the item:

  Heavenly Hughes, representing My TRIBE Rise
  Jane Ward, representing Showing Up for Racial Justice

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

Councilmembers Comments  Councilmember Kennedy stated that he would like to agendize
  at a future joint meeting with Supervisor Barger a discussion on
  the City's water issues (i.e. safe and affordable drinking water,
  adequate water supplies, reservoir water project); costs
  associated with renovating the Pasadena Central Library and
  the Rose Bowl Stadium; and the need to provide additional
  affordable housing in collaboration with Los Angeles County,
  including vouchers for homeless housing, as well as support for
  the senior housing development project across from City Hall.

  Councilmember Hampton reiterated his request to agendize at a
  future joint meeting with Supervisor Barger a discussion on the
  Los Angeles County's ability to help with the City's mental health
  services to the community including the youth of Pasadena.

  In response to Councilmember Hampton's request, Supervisor
  Barger stated the she will follow up with Jonathan E. Sherin,
  M.D., Director of Los Angeles County Department of Mental
  Health and coordinate with the City Council on providing
  information on how community members can access mental
  health services in the area.

Council Minutes  4  03/30/2022
